description: defk-nbl made each loaded library use its own frame resource type (named after a static's address), so a different library never takes over another's frames and never runs its destructor on a foreign defk_ctx layout. Takeover now only happens for the identical .so. As defence in depth, if that invariant ever changes (shared type name, a separate runtime NIF, etc.), store a layout/version tag (e.g. hash of defk_runtime.h + frame struct size) in each frame and have the destructor and step functions refuse or fail cleanly on a mismatch instead of reading a foreign layout. Low priority while the per-image type holds.

comments.text: Classified nice to have (not a safety gap, not required for the verdict) by 'Which open runtime issues are safety gaps?' (defk-dtw.12).

Design: defk_ctx starts with layout_tag (md5 prefix of defk_runtime.h, emitted as DEFK_HEADER_HASH, xor sizeof(defk_ctx) mix) and frame_size, stamped in defk_promote. Step fns call defk_frame_of (two compares at entry, once per resume) and raise ArgumentError on mismatch. Dtor returns early on a tag mismatch: frees nothing and leaves frames_live alone (leak accepted, no crash). Test seam: __defk_corrupt_tags__/1 flag (like __defk_force_yields__). test/frame_tag_test.exs.

title: Tag frames with a layout version as defence in depth
